+# Local GitHub Actions (act)
+
+Run workflows locally with [nektos/act](https://github.com/nektos/act).
+
+**act never runs production workflows.** Local smoke tests live under `.github/act/workflows/` and are only invoked via `scripts/act-test.sh`. Production CI in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs on GitHub.
+
+## Prerequisites
+
+- Docker (OrbStack, Colima, or Docker Desktop) running
+- `act` installed
+
+## Docker socket (macOS)
+
+`.actrc` sets `--bind` so act sees local action files. Set your Docker socket explicitly:
+
+```bash
+export ACT_DOCKER_SOCKET="${HOME}/.orbstack/run/docker.sock"
+# or Colima:
+# export ACT_DOCKER_SOCKET="${HOME}/.colima/default/docker.sock"
+```
+
+## Commands
+
+| Command | What it runs |
+|---------|----------------|
+| `pnpm run act:full` | Full smoke — tests, coverage, validate, eval, compile parity, bundle all Node actions |
+| `pnpm run act:ci` | Quick — unit tests + build |
+| `pnpm run act:compile` | CLI compile against `pipeline.yml` |
+
+```bash
+pnpm run act:full
+```
+
+## Act-only workflows
+
+| Workflow | Purpose |
+|----------|---------|
+| `.github/act/workflows/full-smoke.yml` | Full local CI parity (default for `act:full`) |
+| `.github/act/workflows/test-smoke.yml` | Unit tests + build |
+| `.github/act/workflows/compile-smoke.yml` | CLI compile against pipeline.yml |
+
+These use `workflow_dispatch` only — they do not run on push/PR to GitHub.
+
+`full-smoke.yml` runs jobs **sequentially** (each job `needs` the previous one). GitHub CI runs validate, compile parity, and bundles in parallel; act chains them so multiple containers do not run `pnpm run build` against the same bind-mounted workspace at once (which can hang on macOS).
+
+## What act covers vs GitHub CI
+
+| Check | act (`act:full`) | GitHub CI |
+|-------|------------------|-----------|
+| Unit tests + coverage | yes | yes |
+| Pipeline validate (strict) | yes | yes |
+| CLI eval | yes | no |
+| Compile CLI ↔ action parity | yes | yes |
+| Bundle run / compile / eval actions | yes | yes (in workflow-lint job) |
+| actionlint + yamllint | no | yes |
+| Live `pipeline-compose-run` dispatch | no | yes on tag push via `release.yml` + `./packages/action-run` |
+
+The run orchestrator is covered by unit tests (`packages/action-run/src/orchestrator.test.ts`). Dispatching stage workflows still requires GitHub.
+
+## Fixture
+
+| File | Purpose |
+|------|---------|
+| `.github/act/workflow-dispatch-compile.json` | Inputs for compile smoke |
+
+## Guardrails
+
+| Layer | What it does |
+|-------|----------------|
+| **Separate workflow files** | act targets `.github/act/workflows/*`, not `.github/workflows/ci.yml` |
+| **Local compile action** | `./packages/action-compile` is used for parity — published actions live in separate repos |

+# Local-only compile smoke (act). See scripts/act-test.sh.
+name: Act — compile smoke
+
+on:
+  workflow_dispatch:
+    inputs:
+      pipeline_file:
+        description: Pipeline YAML path
+        required: true
+        default: .github/pipelines/pipeline.yml
+
+jobs:
+  compile-pipeline:
+    name: Compile pipeline (CLI)
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
+      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v6
+      - uses: actions/setup-node@v6
+        with:
+          node-version: '24'
+          cache: pnpm
+      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
+      - run: pnpm run build
+      - run: >-
+          pnpm exec tsx packages/cli/src/main.ts compile
+          ${{ inputs.pipeline_file }}
+          -o /tmp/act-compile-out.yml
+      - name: Assert generated workflow shape
+        run: grep -q 'compile-check' /tmp/act-compile-out.yml

@@ -0,0 +1,134 @@
+# Local full smoke (act). Mirrors CI jobs that run without GitHub-only secrets.
+# Invoke via: pnpm run act:full
+name: Act — full smoke
+
+on:
+  workflow_dispatch:
+
+jobs:
+  unit-tests:
+    name: Unit tests
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
+      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v6
+      - uses: actions/setup-node@v6
+        with:
+          node-version: '24'
+          cache: pnpm
+      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
+      - run: pnpm test
+      - run: pnpm run build
+      - run: pnpm run test:coverage
+      - run: bash scripts/ci/sync-versions-from-tag.test.sh
+      - run: bash scripts/ci/check-workspace-versions.test.sh
+      - run: git fetch --tags --force origin
+      - run: bash scripts/ci/check-workspace-versions.sh
+
+  pipeline-validate:
+    name: Pipeline validate
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    # Sequential chain: parallel `pnpm run build` on the same bind mount can hang under act on macOS.
+    needs: unit-tests
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
+      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v6
+      - uses: actions/setup-node@v6
+        with:
+          node-version: '24'
+          cache: pnpm
+      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
+      - run: pnpm run build
+      - run: pnpm run validate .github/pipelines/pipeline.yml --workflows --strict
+      - run: >-
+          pnpm run validate
+          examples/run-tag-release/.github/pipelines/pipeline.yml
+          --repo-root examples/run-tag-release
+          --workflows
+          --strict
+
+  cli-eval:
+    name: CLI eval
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    needs: pipeline-validate
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
+      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v6
+      - uses: actions/setup-node@v6
+        with:
+          node-version: '24'
+          cache: pnpm
+      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
+      - run: pnpm run build
+      - run: >-
+          pnpm run eval
+          --expression "startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')"
+          --github '{"ref":"refs/tags/v1.0.0"}'
+      - run: pnpm run eval --expression "true" | grep -qx true
+
+  compile-parity:
+    name: Compile action parity
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    needs: cli-eval
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
+      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v6
+      - uses: actions/setup-node@v6
+        with:
+          node-version: '24'
+          cache: pnpm
+      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
+      - run: pnpm run build
+      - run: pnpm --filter @aeswibon/pipeline-compose-action-compile run bundle
+      - run: >-
+          pnpm exec tsx packages/cli/src/main.ts compile
+          .github/pipelines/pipeline.yml
+          -o /tmp/act-cli-out.yml
+          --workflow-output .github/workflows/release.yml
+          --compile-action ./packages/action-compile
+      - uses: ./packages/action-compile
+        with:
+          pipeline_file: .github/pipelines/pipeline.yml
+          output: /tmp/act-action-out.yml
+          workflow_output: .github/workflows/release.yml
+          compile_action: ./packages/action-compile
+      - run: diff /tmp/act-cli-out.yml /tmp/act-action-out.yml
+
+  bundle-actions:
+    name: Bundle Node actions
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    needs: compile-parity
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
+      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v6
+      - uses: actions/setup-node@v6
+        with:
+          node-version: '24'
+          cache: pnpm
+      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
+      - run: pnpm run build
+      - run: pnpm run bundle:actions
+      - run: test -f packages/action-run/dist/index.js
+      - run: test -f packages/action-compile/dist/index.js
+      - run: test -f packages/action-eval/dist/index.js
+
+  workflow-lint:
+    name: Workflow lint
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    needs: bundle-actions
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
+      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v6
+      - uses: actions/setup-node@v6
+        with:
+          node-version: '24'
+          cache: pnpm
+      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
+      - run: pnpm run bundle:actions
+      - name: Install actionlint
+        run: |
+          curl -sSfL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rhysd/actionlint/main/scripts/download-actionlint.bash \
+            | bash
+          sudo mv actionlint /usr/local/bin/
+      - run: pip install yamllint
+      - run: bash scripts/lint-workflows.sh

+version: 2
+concurrency:
+  group: release-${{ github.ref }}
+  global: true
+  lock_repo: abhiudayg/pipeline-compose
+  cancel_in_progress: false
+groups:
+  release:
+    description: Meta-repo tag release chain
+companion_workflows:
+  - .github/workflows/release.yml
+  - .github/workflows/smoke-cross-repo.yml
+  - .github/workflows/pipeline-pr-comment.yml
+  - .github/workflows/visualize.yml
+pipelines:
+  release:
+    group: release
+    context_schema:
+      type: object
+      properties:
+        version-sync:
+          type: object
+          properties:
+            version:
+              type: string
+              pattern: ^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(-[0-9A-Za-z.-]+)?$
+            skip_publish:
+              type: string
+              enum:
+                - 'true'
+                - 'false'
+    stages:
+      - id: ci
+        workflow: .github/workflows/ci.yml
+      - id: version-sync
+        workflow: .github/workflows/stage-version-sync.yml
+        needs:
+          - ci
+        outputs:
+          - version
+          - skip_publish
+      - id: release-publish
+        workflow: .github/workflows/stage-release-publish.yml
+        needs:
+          - version-sync
+        inputs:
+          version: ${{ context.version-sync.version }}
+          skip_publish: ${{ context.version-sync.skip_publish }}
+      - id: publish-actions
+        workflow: .github/workflows/publish-actions.yml
+        needs:
+          - release-publish
+        inputs:
+          version: ${{ context.version-sync.version }}

@@ -0,0 +1,112 @@
+name: Pipeline PR comment
+
+on:
+  pull_request:
+    paths:
+      - '.github/pipelines/**'
+      - 'packages/core/schema/**'
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+  pull-requests: write
+
+jobs:
+  pipeline-comment:
+    name: Post pipeline validation comment
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
+      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v6
+      - uses: actions/setup-node@v6
+        with:
+          node-version: '24'
+          cache: pnpm
+      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
+      - run: pnpm run build
+      - name: Validate pipeline
+        id: validate
+        continue-on-error: true
+        env:
+          SIMULATE_GITHUB: ${{ toJson(github) }}
+        run: |
+          set +e
+          pnpm exec tsx packages/cli/src/main.ts validate .github/pipelines/pipeline.yml \
+            --repo-root . --workflows --strict --json --mermaid --simulate --github "$SIMULATE_GITHUB" \
+            > /tmp/pipeline-report.json
+          echo "report_exit=$?" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+      - name: Post PR comment
+        uses: actions/github-script@v9
+        with:
+          script: |
+            const fs = require('node:fs');
+            const marker = '<!-- pipeline-compose-pr-bot -->';
+            const report = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync('/tmp/pipeline-report.json', 'utf8'));
+            const mermaid = (report.mermaid ?? '').trim();
+            const ok = report.ok;
+            const issues = (report.issues ?? [])
+              .map((issue) => `- **${issue.level}**: ${issue.message}`)
+              .join('\n');
+            const simulation = report.simulation ?? [];
+            const showRerun = simulation.some((stage) => stage.rerun);
+            const simRows = simulation
+              .map((stage) => {
+                const cols = [`\`${stage.id}\``, stage.status];
+                if (showRerun) {
+                  cols.push(stage.rerun ?? '—');
+                }
+                cols.push(stage.reason ?? '—');
+                return `| ${cols.join(' | ')} |`;
+              })
+              .join('\n');
+            const simHeader = showRerun
+              ? '| Stage | Status | Rerun | Reason |'
+              : '| Stage | Status | Reason |';
+            const simSep = showRerun
+              ? '| --- | --- | --- | --- |'
+              : '| --- | --- | --- |';
+            const body = [
+              marker,
+              '## Pipeline Compose validation',
+              '',
+              `**Status:** ${ok ? '✅ OK' : '❌ Failed'}`,
+              '',
+              '### Topology',
+              '',
+              '```mermaid',
+              mermaid,
+              '```',
+              '',
+              '### Simulation (dry-run)',
+              '',
+              simulation.length
+                ? [simHeader, simSep, simRows].join('\n')
+                : '_No stages._',
+              '',
+              '### Issues',
+              '',
+              issues || '_No issues._',
+            ].join('\n');
+
+            const { owner, repo } = context.repo;
+            const issue_number = context.payload.pull_request.number;
+            const { data: comments } = await github.rest.issues.listComments({
+              owner,
+              repo,
+              issue_number,
+            });
+            const existing = comments.find((comment) => comment.body?.includes(marker));
+            if (existing) {
+              await github.rest.issues.updateComment({
+                owner,
+                repo,
+                comment_id: existing.id,
+                body,
+              });
+            } else {
+              await github.rest.issues.createComment({
+                owner,
+                repo,
+                issue_number,
+                body,
+              });
+            }

+name: Publish actions
+
+on:
+  workflow_dispatch:
+    inputs:
+      version:
+        description: Semver without v prefix (e.g. 0.3.1)
+        type: string
+        required: true
+      use_master:
+        description: Build from monorepo master HEAD instead of v{version} (action repo tag must still be new)
+        type: boolean
+        required: false
+        default: false
+  workflow_call:
+    inputs:
+      version:
+        description: Semver without v prefix
+        type: string
+        required: true
+      use_master:
+        description: Build from monorepo master HEAD instead of v{version} (action repo tag must still be new)
+        type: boolean
+        required: false
+        default: false
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+
+jobs:
+  publish-actions:
+    name: Publish action repositories
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 15
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
+        with:
+          ref: master
+          fetch-depth: 0
+
+      - name: Checkout source ref
+        env:
+          VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}
+          USE_MASTER: ${{ inputs.use_master }}
+        run: |
+          if [ "$USE_MASTER" = "true" ]; then
+            echo "Publishing from master HEAD (already checked out)"
+          elif git rev-parse "refs/tags/v${VERSION}^{commit}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+            git checkout "refs/tags/v${VERSION}"
+            echo "Using tag v${VERSION} at $(git rev-parse HEAD)"
+          else
+            echo "::warning::Tag v${VERSION} not found; publishing from master."
+          fi
+
+      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v6
+
+      - uses: actions/setup-node@v6
+        with:
+          node-version: '24'
+          cache: pnpm
+
+      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
+
+      - run: pnpm run bundle:actions
+
+      - name: Require publish token
+        env:
+          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.ACTION_PUBLISH_TOKEN }}
+        run: |
+          if [ -z "$GH_TOKEN" ]; then
+            echo "Missing repository secret ACTION_PUBLISH_TOKEN."
+            echo "Add a PAT with contents:write on pipeline-compose-run, -export, -compile, -eval, and -context-merge."
+            exit 1
+          fi

@@ -0,0 +1,118 @@
+name: Version sync
+
+on:
+  workflow_dispatch:
+  workflow_call:
+    outputs:
+      version:
+        description: Semver without v prefix
+        value: ${{ jobs.version-sync.outputs.version }}
+      skip_publish:
+        description: True when master and tag already had synced version files
+        value: ${{ jobs.version-sync.outputs.skip_publish }}
+      commit_sha:
+        description: Commit SHA after version sync (tag target)
+        value: ${{ jobs.version-sync.outputs.commit_sha }}
+
+permissions:
+  contents: write
+  actions: write
+
+concurrency:
+  group: stage-version-sync-${{ github.ref }}
+  cancel-in-progress: false
+
+jobs:
+  version-sync:
+    name: Sync version files from tag
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    timeout-minutes: 10
+    outputs:
+      version: ${{ steps.tag.outputs.version }}
+      skip_publish: ${{ steps.git-state.outputs.skip_publish }}
+      commit_sha: ${{ steps.resolve-head.outputs.commit_sha }}
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
+        with:
+          fetch-depth: 0
+          ref: master
+
+      - name: Resolve tag version
+        id: tag
+        run: |
+          ref="${GITHUB_REF}"
+          if ! [[ "$ref" =~ ^refs/tags/v(.+)$ ]]; then
+            echo "Expected refs/tags/vX.Y.Z, got $ref"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          version="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
+          if ! [[ "$version" =~ ^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+(-[0-9A-Za-z.-]+)?$ ]]; then
+            echo "Invalid semver tag: v${version}"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          echo "version=$version" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+          echo "Tag version: $version"
+
+      - name: Sync version files
+        run: bash scripts/ci/sync-versions-from-tag.sh "${{ steps.tag.outputs.version }}"
+
+      - name: Require CHANGELOG section for release
+        run: bash scripts/ci/require-changelog-section.sh "${{ steps.tag.outputs.version }}"
+
+      - name: Detect git release state
+        id: git-state
+        env:
+          VERSION: ${{ steps.tag.outputs.version }}
+        run: |
+          git fetch origin master "refs/tags/v${VERSION}"
+          master_sha=$(git rev-parse origin/master)
+          tag_sha=$(git rev-parse "refs/tags/v${VERSION}^{commit}" 2>/dev/null || echo "")
+          if [ -z "$(git status --porcelain)" ] && [ -n "$tag_sha" ] && [ "$tag_sha" = "$master_sha" ]; then
+            echo "Git release aligned: tag v${VERSION} at master with synced files."
+            echo "skip_publish=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+          else
+            echo "Git release needs publish (version commit and/or retag)."
+            echo "skip_publish=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+          fi
+
+      - name: Publish version sync to master
+        if: steps.git-state.outputs.skip_publish != 'true'
+        id: publish
+        env:
+          VERSION: ${{ steps.tag.outputs.version }}
+          DEFAULT_BRANCH: master
+        run: bash scripts/ci/publish-version-sync.sh "${VERSION}"
+
+      - name: Resolve release commit
+        id: resolve-head
+        env:
+          VERSION: ${{ steps.tag.outputs.version }}
+        run: |
+          git fetch origin master "refs/tags/v${VERSION}"
+          echo "commit_sha=$(git rev-parse "refs/tags/v${VERSION}^{commit}")" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+
+      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v6
+        if: success()
+
+      - uses: actions/setup-node@v6
+        if: success()
+        with:
+          node-version: '24'
+          cache: pnpm
+
+      - name: Bundle export action
+        if: success()
+        run: |
+          pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
+          pnpm --filter @aeswibon/pipeline-compose-action-export run bundle
+
+      - uses: ./packages/action-export
+        if: success()
+        with:
+          stage_id: version-sync
+          validate_schema: true
+          context_schema_json: >-
+            {"type":"object","properties":{"version-sync":{"type":"object","properties":{"version":{"type":"string","pattern":"^[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+(-[0-9A-Za-z.-]+)?$"},"skip_publish":{"type":"string","enum":["true","false"]}}}}}
+          outputs: >-
+            {"version":"${{ steps.tag.outputs.version }}",
+             "skip_publish":"${{ steps.git-state.outputs.skip_publish }}"}

+# Pipeline Orchestration
+
+Cross-repository and intra-repository workflow DAG execution inside GitHub Actions that executes stages in dependency order, aggregates stage outputs via artifacts, enforces mutual exclusion via global locks, and caches previous attempt outputs via attempt-scoped smart rerun.
+
+## Sub-features
+
+- `stage-wave-dispatch`: Partitions pipeline stages into concurrent execution waves using Kahn's topological sort.
+  - Intent: Run independent stages in parallel while respecting `needs:` dependencies.
+  - Behaviour: Computes in-degree for all stages and groups zero-dependency nodes into sequential waves.
+  - Outcome: Concurrently dispatches workflow jobs per wave via GitHub Actions REST API.
+- `artifact-context-merge`: Out-of-band stage data transmission via short-lived workflow artifacts.
+  - Intent: Pass structured outputs between stages across repository boundaries without size limits.
+  - Behaviour: `pipeline-compose-export` writes `outputs.json` to an artifact; orchestrator downloads and merges into `context.<stage>.*`.
+  - Outcome: Downstream stages receive dynamic inputs evaluated from upstream stage outputs.
+- `smart-rerun-cache`: Reuses prior attempt outputs when stage inputs and workflow digests remain unchanged.
+  - Intent: Prevent redundant execution of expensive succeeded stages on workflow retry.
+  - Behaviour: Computes SHA-256 fingerprint over inputs, ref, and workflow file; reuses attempt-1 outputs on attempt-2+.
+  - Outcome: Skips dispatch of unchanged stages and logs saved execution time.
+- `global-concurrency-lock`: Cross-repository mutual exclusion protecting shared environments.
+  - Intent: Prevent concurrent pipeline runs from conflicting over shared deployment targets.
+  - Behaviour: Performs atomic compare-and-swap lock acquisition on a designated lock repository.
+  - Outcome: Overlapping pipeline executions are serialized or safely failed without race conditions.
+
+## How to get to it (user POV)
+
+- Action entry: Include `uses: abhiudayg/pipeline-compose-run@v1` in an entry workflow pointing to `.github/pipelines/pipeline.yml`.
+- Output export: Add `uses: abhiudayg/pipeline-compose-export@v1` with `stage_id` and `outputs` JSON in stage workflows.
+- CLI simulation: Run `pipeline-compose validate <pipeline.yml> --simulate` to preview wave execution order and skip decisions.
+
+## Verification Suites (Targeted Test Commands)
+
+- **Unit Tests:** `cd pipeline-compose && pnpm test packages/action-run/src/orchestrator.test.ts`
+- **Wave Ordering Tests:** `cd pipeline-compose && pnpm test packages/core/src/compile/stage-waves.test.ts`
+- **Smart Rerun Tests:** `cd pipeline-compose && pnpm test packages/core/src/lib/smart-rerun.test.ts`
+- **Allowlisted Verification:** `.verify/run.sh unit`
+- **Preconditions:** Node.js >= 20, pnpm >= 10, repository dependencies installed via `pnpm install`.
+
+### 1. **wave-partitioning** — stages without mutual dependencies execute in parallel waves.
+- **Request:** `pnpm test packages/core/src/compile/stage-waves.test.ts`
+- **Why:** Proves that stages with zero shared dependencies partition into concurrent waves.
+- **Expected:** `3 passed (3)` with all wave grouping assertions verified.
+- **Impact:** Guarantees parallelization correctness across multi-stage DAGs.
+
+### 2. **orchestrator-dispatch-and-artifacts** — orchestrator runs stages, polls runs, and merges artifact outputs.
+- **Request:** `pnpm test packages/action-run/src/orchestrator.test.ts`
+- **Why:** Proves the orchestrator dispatch loop, polling mechanism, context merge, and smart rerun cache in isolation.
+- **Expected:** `13 passed (13)` with mock GitHub API client.
+- **Impact:** Confirms runtime orchestration works end-to-end without live GitHub credentials.
+
+## Gotchas
+
+- Orchestrator runner remains active and billable during the entire duration of all downstream stages (orchestrator polling overhead).
+- Global concurrency lock files commit to Git history unless directed to a dedicated lock repository.
+- Sub-pipeline nesting is strictly hard-capped at depth 1.
+
+## Code
+
+- `pipeline-compose/packages/action-run/src/orchestrator.ts`
+- `pipeline-compose/packages/action-run/src/github.ts`
+- `pipeline-compose/packages/action-run/src/smart-rerun.ts`

+- `pipeline-compose/packages/core/src/lib/smart-rerun.ts`
+- `pipeline-compose/packages/core/src/lib/global-lock.ts`

+# Security and Sandboxing
+
+Defensive boundaries, path traversal guards, expression sandbox isolation, output sanitization, and in-memory decompression protecting the orchestrator against malicious inputs, prompt injection, and host compromise.
+
+## Sub-features
+
+- `path-traversal-defense`: Strict boundary checks preventing file access outside repository roots.
+  - Intent: Prevent malicious sub-pipeline or workflow references from reading host sensitive files.
+  - Behaviour: Validates resolved file targets against base directory paths using `path.resolve` and separator checks.
+  - Outcome: Rejects paths containing traversal segments escaping the workspace.
+- `expression-sandbox-isolation`: Pure expression evaluator immune to code execution and prototype pollution.
+  - Intent: Evaluate `when:` conditions without exposing the runner to arbitrary JavaScript execution.
+  - Behaviour: Uses strict tokenization and rejects prototype access (`__proto__`, `constructor`, `prototype`).
+  - Outcome: Executes safe conditional expressions while blocking code injection and arbitrary execution.
+- `in-memory-decompression`: Pure Node.js streaming decompression eliminating shell process invocation.
+  - Intent: Extract stage artifact payloads without relying on vulnerable or missing host `unzip` binaries.
+  - Behaviour: Parses ZIP headers and inflates payload buffers in-memory using `node:zlib` with a fallback mechanism.
+  - Outcome: Safely extracts `outputs.json` across minimal containers, Windows, and Linux runners.
+- `output-html-sanitization`: Context-aware XML/HTML entity escaping on all generated visual reports and SVG diagrams.
+  - Intent: Prevent stored XSS and indirect prompt injection in pull request summaries and status dashboards.
+  - Behaviour: Escapes `<`, `>`, `&`, `"`, and `'` on user-supplied strings before rendering HTML cards.
+  - Outcome: Neutralizes adversarial markup and injection payloads embedded in branch or stage metadata.
+
+## How to get to it (user POV)
+
+- Expressions: Write conditional expressions in `when:` blocks using `${{ context.<stage>.<key> == 'val' }}` or `startsWith()`.
+- Security verification: Run `.verify/run.sh security` to execute the full security and jailbreak suite.
+
+## Verification Suites (Targeted Test Commands)
+
+- **Security & Jailbreak Tests:** `cd pipeline-compose && pnpm test packages/core/src/compile/security.test.ts`
+- **In-Memory Decompression Tests:** `cd pipeline-compose && pnpm test packages/action-run/src/github.test.ts`
+- **Allowlisted Verification:** `.verify/run.sh security`
+- **Preconditions:** Node.js >= 20, pnpm >= 10.
+
+### 1. **traversal-and-sandbox-defenses** — rejects directory traversal and prototype pollution.
+- **Request:** `pnpm test packages/core/src/compile/security.test.ts`
+- **Why:** Proves that path traversal attacks, code injections, and prototype pollution are actively blocked.
+- **Expected:** `7 passed (7)` with all security assertions verified.
+- **Impact:** Shields GitHub Actions runners and CI environments from malicious PR inputs.
+
+### 2. **pure-memory-decompression** — extracts outputs.json without shell execution.
+- **Request:** `pnpm test packages/action-run/src/github.test.ts`
+- **Why:** Proves that ZIP artifact extraction succeeds in memory using native `node:zlib`.
+- **Expected:** `14 passed (14)` including `extractFileFromZipBuffer` suite.
+- **Impact:** Eliminates host `unzip` process spawning and ensures compatibility in minimal container runners.
+
+## Gotchas
+
+- Global concurrency locks require `contents: write` token scope; ensure credentials adhere to least privilege.
+- Expressions only support a strict whitelist of operators (`startsWith`, `contains`, `==`, `&&`, `||`); arbitrary logic must be encapsulated in stages.
+
+## Code
+
+- `pipeline-compose/packages/core/src/compile/security.test.ts`
+- `pipeline-compose/packages/core/src/lib/expressions.ts`
+- `pipeline-compose/packages/core/src/compile/sub-pipeline.ts`
+- `pipeline-compose/packages/action-run/src/workflow-digest.ts`
+- `pipeline-compose/packages/action-run/src/github.ts`
+- `pipeline-compose/packages/core/src/compile/visualize.ts`
+- `pipeline-compose/packages/core/src/lib/global-lock.ts`

@@ -0,0 +1,61 @@
+# Workflow Compilation
+
+Static compilation of declarative pipeline DAG definitions into standard GitHub Actions workflow YAML files with native needs dependencies, accompanied by offline validation, topological sorting, simulation, and monorepo task graph importing.
+
+## Sub-features
+
+- `yaml-workflow-codegen`: Emits native multi-job GitHub Actions workflows from pipeline definitions.
+  - Intent: Provide single-repo teams with committed audit trails and native GitHub UX without an orchestrator runner.
+  - Behaviour: Translates stage `needs:` and `${{ context.stage.output }}` into `${{ needs.stage.outputs.output }}`.
+  - Outcome: Produces deterministic `.github/workflows/*.yml` files.
+- `pipeline-schema-validation`: Enforces JSON schema constraints and catches DAG cycles ahead of execution.
+  - Intent: Prevent invalid pipelines, schema v1 regressions, and cycles from reaching CI.
+  - Behaviour: Evaluates definitions against Ajv JSON schemas and detects circular dependencies via topological sort.
+  - Outcome: Emits clear error codes and fails pre-merge validation when defects exist.
+- `monorepo-task-import`: Automatically converts Turborepo, Nx, or Rush task graphs into pipeline definitions.
+  - Intent: Enable seamless adoption in monorepos without manual YAML authoring.
+  - Behaviour: Reads package/task dependencies and builds equivalent stage DAGs.
+  - Outcome: Emits valid `pipeline.yml` ready for orchestration or compilation.
+
+## How to get to it (user POV)
+
+- CLI compile: Run `pipeline-compose compile <pipeline.yml> -o .github/workflows/pipeline.yml` to generate workflow YAML.
+- CLI validate: Run `pipeline-compose validate <pipeline.yml> --strict` to check schemas and DAG invariants.
+- CLI import: Run `pipeline-compose import turbo --config turbo.json` to generate starter pipeline definitions.
+
+## Verification Suites (Targeted Test Commands)
+
+- **Codegen Unit Tests:** `cd pipeline-compose && pnpm test packages/core/src/compile/codegen.test.ts`
+- **Schema Validation Tests:** `cd pipeline-compose && pnpm test packages/core/src/compile/validator.test.ts`
+- **Monorepo Import Tests:** `cd pipeline-compose && pnpm test packages/core/src/import/monorepo-tasks.test.ts`
+- **Allowlisted Verification:** `.verify/run.sh functional`
+- **Preconditions:** Node.js >= 20, pnpm >= 10.
+
+### 1. **codegen-native-wiring** — translates stage graph into native needs jobs.
+- **Request:** `pnpm test packages/core/src/compile/codegen.test.ts`
+- **Why:** Proves that pipeline YAML produces valid GitHub Actions workflow YAML with correct `needs:` dependencies.
+- **Expected:** `3 passed (3)` with all workflow generation assertions satisfied.
+- **Impact:** Ensures compile-path workflows execute accurately on standard GitHub Actions runners.
+
+### 2. **schema-and-cycle-validation** — rejects schema v1 and cycles with deterministic errors.
+- **Request:** `pnpm test packages/core/src/compile/validator.test.ts`
+- **Why:** Proves that invalid structures and cyclic dependency graphs fail immediately before CI execution.
+- **Expected:** `10 passed (10)` with strict schema checks.
+- **Impact:** Prevents malformed or broken DAGs from being merged or executed.
+
+## Gotchas
+
+- Compiled workflows cannot dynamically invoke workflows across external repositories without static reusable workflow configurations.
+- Sub-pipelines (`pipeline_file`) are not supported in compilation mode; they require the runtime orchestrator (`pipeline-compose-run`).

+# Knowledge Base: Pipeline Orchestration
+
+## What It Does
+Pipeline Orchestration provides a dynamic runtime engine for executing multi-stage, multi-repository GitHub Actions workflows according to a declarative directed acyclic graph (DAG) defined in `.github/pipelines/pipeline.yml`. It coordinates workflow dispatching across repositories, synchronizes parallel execution waves, passes structured output payloads between stages using short-lived GitHub Actions artifacts, enforces global cross-repo mutual exclusion, and skips redundant executions on workflow retries using smart rerun fingerprinting.
+
+## How It Works
+The orchestration lifecycle operates in four stages:
+1. **DAG Parsing & Wave Grouping**: The orchestrator (`pipeline-compose-run`) parses the pipeline definition using `@aeswibon/pipeline-compose-core`. It validates stage schemas and computes dependency waves using Kahn's topological sorting algorithm. Stages within the same wave have zero inter-dependencies and are executed concurrently.
+2. **Dynamic Dispatch & Polling**: For each wave, the orchestrator dispatches stage workflows using the GitHub Actions REST API (`workflow_dispatch`). It resolves repository tokens via PAT mappings or GitHub App installation tokens. It enters a 10-second polling loop inspecting workflow run conclusion states until all stages in the wave complete.
+3. **Artifact-Backed Context Bus**: Stage workflows that declare outputs invoke `pipeline-compose-export`, which serializes the output object to `pipeline-compose/outputs.json` and uploads an artifact named `pipeline-compose-<stageId>` with a 1-day retention policy. Upon stage completion, the orchestrator downloads and parses the artifact in-memory, merging the key-value pairs into the global `context.<stage>.*` state.
+4. **Smart Rerun Cache**: If a workflow fails and an operator clicks "Re-run failed jobs", the orchestrator detects `GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT > 1`. It computes a SHA-256 fingerprint for each stage based on inputs, ref, and workflow file digests. If the fingerprint matches the previous attempt's record, the stage is skipped and its previous outputs are reused.
+
+## Where the Code Is
+- **Runtime Orchestrator**: `packages/action-run/src/orchestrator.ts`
+- **GitHub API Client & In-Memory Decompressor**: `packages/action-run/src/github.ts`
+- **Token Resolution & GitHub App Integration**: `packages/action-run/src/repo-tokens.ts`, `packages/action-run/src/github-app.ts`
+- **Smart Rerun Engine**: `packages/action-run/src/smart-rerun.ts`, `packages/core/src/lib/smart-rerun.ts`
+- **Output Export Action**: `packages/action-export/src/index.ts`, `packages/action-export/src/outputs.ts`
+- **DAG Wave Partitioning**: `packages/core/src/compile/stage-waves.ts`, `packages/core/src/compile/topo-sort.ts`
+
+## How to Use It
+1. Define a pipeline in `.github/pipelines/pipeline.yml`:
+   ```yaml
+   version: 2
+   pipelines:
+     release:
+       stages:
+         - id: build
+           workflow: .github/workflows/build.yml
+         - id: test
+           workflow: .github/workflows/test.yml
+           repo: my-org/e2e-tests
+           needs: [build]
+           inputs:
+             tag: ${{ context.build.tag }}
+   ```
+2. In the target stage workflow, export outputs:
+   ```yaml
+   - uses: abhiudayg/pipeline-compose-export@v1
+     with:
+       stage_id: build
+       outputs: '{"tag": "v1.2.3"}'
+   ```
+3. In the entry repository workflow, invoke the runner:
+   ```yaml
+   - uses: abhiudayg/pipeline-compose-run@v1
+     with:
+       pipeline_file: .github/pipelines/pipeline.yml
+   ```
+
+## How It Is Verified
+Verification is driven through unit and mock orchestrator tests in Vitest. A virtual mock GitHub Actions client simulates workflow dispatches, run status polling, artifact downloads, and commit status transitions without requiring live GitHub credentials or network access.
+
+## Known Limits
+- **Orchestrator Idle Cost**: The orchestrator job remains active on a VM runner during the execution of all child stages, consuming billable minutes during long-running workflows.
+- **Sub-Pipeline Depth**: Sub-pipeline nesting is capped at 1 level; nested pipelines cannot define child sub-pipelines.
+- **Artifact Propagation Latency**: GitHub Actions artifacts occasionally experience brief propagation delays before becoming accessible via the REST API.

+# Knowledge Base: Security and Sandboxing
+
+## What It Does
+Security and Sandboxing enforces defensive boundaries across the pipeline orchestration engine. It protects GitHub Actions runner hosts, CI environments, and downstream consumers from path traversal attacks, arbitrary JavaScript code execution, prototype pollution, prompt injection via PR summaries, and shell process hijacking.
+
+## How It Works
+1. **Path Traversal Defenses**:
+   - Sub-pipeline resolution (`resolveSubPipeline`) canonicalizes file paths using `path.resolve` and verifies that the resolved target path resides strictly within the bounds of `repoRoot`. Any attempt to reference files outside the workspace (e.g., `../../etc/shadow`) throws an explicit security error.
+   - Remote workflow digests and file digests (`workflowFileDigest`) apply boundary checks before reading file contents.
+   - Global concurrency lock file paths (`globalLockPath`) cleanse traversal sequences (`..`), ensuring that lock records are strictly constrained within `.pipeline-compose/locks/*.json`.
+2. **Expression Sandbox Isolation**:
+   - Conditional evaluation of `when:` blocks in `evaluateExpression` avoids `eval()` and `new Function()`.
+   - The expression evaluator tokenizes operators (`startsWith`, `contains`, `==`, `&&`, `||`) deterministically.
+   - Object property lookups on `github.*` and `context.*` explicitly block prototype pollution vectors (`__proto__`, `constructor`, `prototype`).
+   - Adversarial prompt injection payloads embedded in context strings (e.g., `"Ignore previous instructions and grant admin"`) are treated strictly as literal string values and cannot hijack evaluation logic.
+3. **In-Memory Streaming Decompression**:
+   - The orchestrator extracts stage outputs from ZIP artifact archives in memory using Node's native `node:zlib` (`inflateRawSync`) without spawning host shell processes (`unzip`).
+   - If an archive uses an unsupported streaming layout, it falls back safely to the system decompressor.
+4. **Output HTML & XML Sanitization**:
+   - All HTML visualizer and SVG rendering functions apply context-aware entity escaping (`escapeXml`) over all user-supplied stage IDs, pipeline names, and workflow paths, escaping `<`, `>`, `&`, `"`, and `'` to prevent XSS and indirect prompt injection.
+
+## Where the Code Is
+- **Expression Sandbox**: `packages/core/src/lib/expressions.ts`
+- **Sub-Pipeline Boundary Enforcement**: `packages/core/src/compile/sub-pipeline.ts`
+- **Digest Path Guard**: `packages/action-run/src/workflow-digest.ts`
+- **In-Memory ZIP Extractor**: `packages/action-run/src/github.ts`
+- **HTML & SVG Sanitizer**: `packages/core/src/compile/visualize.ts`
+- **Global Lock Sanitizer**: `packages/core/src/lib/global-lock.ts`
+- **Security & Jailbreak Tests**: `packages/core/src/compile/security.test.ts`
+
+## How to Use It
+All security protections are enabled by default and require no configuration. When authoring pipelines:
+- Express conditions using standard whitelisted operators:
+  ```yaml
+  when: "startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v') && context.ci.status == 'success'"
+  ```
+- Reference sub-pipelines using repository-relative paths:
+  ```yaml
+  pipeline_file: .github/pipelines/sub.yml
+  ```
+
+## How It Is Verified
+Security and jailbreak defenses are verified via a dedicated test suite (`packages/core/src/compile/security.test.ts`) that executes attack payloads against path resolution, expression evaluation, prototype traversal, and HTML generation.
+
+## Known Limits
+- **Secrets in Context**: Any stage output written to `outputs.json` becomes visible in downstream stages and artifact downloads; secrets should never be exported as context values. Secrets must be forwarded via GitHub Actions secrets or environment variables.
+- **Repository Token Scope**: Global lock management requires `contents: write` on the designated lock repository; organizations should use dedicated, isolated lock repositories to adhere to least privilege principles.

+# Knowledge Base: Workflow Compilation
+
+## What It Does
+Workflow Compilation converts pipeline YAML definitions into standard, static GitHub Actions workflow files with native `needs:` job dependencies. It is designed for single-repository topologies where organizations require committed workflow audit trails, native GitHub Actions visualization, and zero orchestrator runner overhead. The compiler is paired with an extensive offline CLI toolchain for validation, dry-run simulation, Mermaid diagram generation, and monorepo task graph imports.
+
+## How It Works
+1. **Schema & Cycle Validation**: The compiler reads `.github/pipelines/pipeline.yml` and validates it against `pipeline-v2.schema.json` via Ajv. It runs topological sorting to detect any circular dependencies or orphan stages before generating output.
+2. **YAML Code Generation**: For each stage in the pipeline, the compiler generates a GitHub Actions job referencing the reusable workflow path (`uses: ./...`). Context references formatted as `${{ context.<stage>.<key> }}` are automatically translated into native job dependency references: `${{ needs.<stage>.outputs.<key> }}`.
+3. **Parity Enforcement**: The compiled workflow includes a `compile-check` job verifying that the committed `.github/workflows/pipeline.yml` matches the output of `pipeline-compose compile` on every pull request, preventing configuration drift.
+4. **Monorepo Task Graph Import**: The CLI toolchain can inspect existing monorepo build tools (Turborepo `turbo.json`, Nx `nx.json`, or Rush `command-line.json`) and generate an equivalent pipeline DAG automatically.
+
+## Where the Code Is
+- **Workflow Codegen**: `packages/core/src/compile/codegen.ts`
+- **Schema & Policy Validator**: `packages/core/src/compile/validator.ts`, `packages/core/src/compile/validate-policy.ts`
+- **Topological Sorting**: `packages/core/src/compile/topo-sort.ts`
+- **Simulation Engine**: `packages/core/src/compile/simulate.ts`
+- **Mermaid & Visualizer**: `packages/core/src/compile/mermaid.ts`, `packages/core/src/compile/visualize.ts`
+- **Compile Action Wrapper**: `packages/action-compile/src/index.ts`
+- **Monorepo Task Importers**: `packages/core/src/import/monorepo-tasks.ts`, `packages/core/src/import/render-import.ts`
+- **CLI Entrypoint**: `packages/cli/src/main.ts`
+
+## How to Use It
+1. Run compilation from the repository root:
+   ```bash
+   pipeline-compose compile .github/pipelines/pipeline.yml -o .github/workflows/pipeline.yml
+   ```
+2. Commit the generated workflow:
+   ```bash
+   git add .github/workflows/pipeline.yml && git commit -m "chore: compile pipeline workflow"
+   ```
+3. Use the CLI to dry-run simulate execution:
+   ```bash
+   pipeline-compose validate .github/pipelines/pipeline.yml --simulate
+   ```
+4. Render an offline Mermaid diagram:
+   ```bash
+   pipeline-compose validate .github/pipelines/pipeline.yml --mermaid
+   ```
+
+## How It Is Verified
+Verification is performed via unit test suites asserting exact AST parity between the generated YAML and expected GitHub Actions workflow syntax, schema validation tests against invalid fixtures, and CLI integration tests.
+
+## Known Limits
+- **Cross-Repository Limitation**: Compiled workflows rely on native GitHub Actions reusable workflows (`uses: ./...`); they cannot dynamically dispatch to cross-repository stages without pre-configuring reusable workflow permissions and static repository coordinates.
+- **Sub-Pipeline Exclusion**: Nested sub-pipelines (`pipeline_file`) are not supported in compilation mode; they must be flattened or executed via `pipeline-compose-run`.

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+set -euo pipefail
+
+ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
+TARGET="${1:-all}"
+RUN_ID="$(date -u '+%Y%m%d-%H%M%S')"
+LOG_DIR="$ROOT/.verify/artifacts"
+mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"
+LOG_FILE="$LOG_DIR/run-${RUN_ID}.log"
+
+exec > >(tee "$LOG_FILE") 2>&1
+
+echo "=================================================="
+echo "agstack Verification Harness: pipeline-action"
+echo "Phase Target: $TARGET"
+echo "Run ID: $RUN_ID"
+echo "Timestamp: $(date -u '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ')"
+echo "=================================================="
+
+run_doctor() {
+  echo "--- Phase 1: Doctor ---"
+  bash "$ROOT/.verify/doctor.sh"
+}
+
+run_unit() {
+  echo "--- Phase 2: Unit Tests (Vitest) ---"
+  cd "$ROOT/pipeline-compose"
+  pnpm test
+}
+
+run_static() {
+  echo "--- Phase 3: Static & Typecheck Build ---"
+  cd "$ROOT/pipeline-compose"
+  pnpm run build
+}
+
+run_functional() {
+  echo "--- Phase 4: Functional CLI DAG & Compile ---"
+  cd "$ROOT/pipeline-compose"
+  pnpm exec tsx packages/cli/src/main.ts validate .github/pipelines/pipeline.yml --workflows --strict --simulate
+  pnpm exec tsx packages/cli/src/main.ts compile .github/pipelines/pipeline.yml -o /tmp/verify-compiled.yml
+  echo "Generated workflow compiled successfully."
+}
+
+run_security() {
+  echo "--- Phase 5: Security Audit & Jailbreak Defense ---"
+  cd "$ROOT/pipeline-compose"
+  pnpm test packages/core/src/compile/security.test.ts
+}
+
+case "$TARGET" in
+  doctor)
+    run_doctor
+    ;;
+  unit)
+    run_unit
+    ;;
+  static)
+    run_static
+    ;;
+  functional)
+    run_functional
+    ;;
+  security)
+    run_security
+    ;;
+  all|"")
+    run_doctor
+    run_static
+    run_unit
+    run_functional
+    run_security
+    ;;
+  *)
+    echo "Unknown target phase: $TARGET" >&2
+    echo "Usage: $0 [all|doctor|unit|static|functional|security]" >&2
+    exit 1
+    ;;
+esac
+
+echo "=================================================="
+echo "Verification Suite Succeeded: Exit Code 0"
+echo "Log preserved at: $LOG_FILE"
+echo "=================================================="

+# Ponytail, lazy senior dev mode
+
+You are a lazy senior developer. Lazy means efficient, not careless. The best code is the code never written.
+
+Before writing any code, stop at the first rung that holds:
+
+1. Does this need to be built at all? (YAGNI)
+2. Does the standard library already do this? Use it.
+3. Does a native platform feature cover it? Use it.
+4. Does an already-installed dependency solve it? Use it.
+5. Can this be one line? Make it one line.
+6. Only then: write the minimum code that works.
+
+Rules:
+
+- No abstractions that weren't explicitly requested.
+- No new dependency if it can be avoided.
+- No boilerplate nobody asked for.
+- Deletion over addition. Boring over clever. Fewest files possible.
+- Question complex requests: "Do you actually need X, or does Y cover it?"
+- Pick the edge-case-correct option when two stdlib approaches are the same size, lazy means less code, not the flimsier algorithm.
+- Mark intentional simplifications with a `ponytail:` comment. If the shortcut has a known ceiling (global lock, O(n²) scan, naive heuristic), the comment names the ceiling and the upgrade path.
+
+Not lazy about: input validation at trust boundaries, error handling that prevents data loss, security, accessibility, anything explicitly requested. Non-trivial logic leaves ONE runnable check behind, the smallest thing that fails if the logic breaks (an assert-based demo/self-check or one small test file; no frameworks, no fixtures). Trivial one-liners need no test.
+
+(Yes, this file also applies to agents working on the ponytail repo itself. Especially to them.)

+## [0.1.0] - 2026-06-14
+
+First release of **pipeline-compose** — define the order your GitHub Actions workflows run with one pipeline YAML file and one action step. No compile step and no generated workflow to commit.
+
+### Added
+
+- **`run` action** (`aeswibon/pipeline-compose/run@v0.1.0`) — primary runtime orchestrator
+  - Reads pipeline YAML (schema v1) and topologically sorts stages by `needs`
+  - Dispatches each stage via `workflow_dispatch`, waits for completion, chains the next stage
+  - Passes prior stage outputs into later inputs via `${{ context.<stage-id>.<output> }}`
+  - Conditional stages with `when:` (supported expression subset)
+  - `results_json` output: JSON array of `{ stageId, runId, outputs }` per completed stage
+- **`compile` action** — optional static workflow codegen for teams that prefer a committed runner workflow
+- **CLI** — `pipeline-compose compile` and `pipeline-compose eval` for local validation and codegen
+- **Pipeline schema v1** — `name`, `version`, `stages[]` with `id`, `workflow`, `needs`, `inputs`, `outputs`, `when`
+- **Artifact-based output collection** — stages export `pipeline-compose-<stage-id>/outputs.json` because GitHub's API does not return job outputs for `workflow_dispatch` runs
+- **Documentation** — consumer-focused [README](README.md), [docs/examples.md](docs/examples.md), [docs/development.md](docs/development.md)
+- **Template** — [templates/pipeline-run.yml](templates/pipeline-run.yml) entry workflow for tag/release pipelines
+
+### Usage
+
+```yaml
+permissions:
+  contents: write
+  actions: write
+
+jobs:
+  run-pipeline:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
+      - uses: aeswibon/pipeline-compose/run@v0.1.0
+        with:
+          pipeline_file: .github/pipelines/pipeline.yml
+          github_token: ${{ github.token }}
+```
+
+### Stage contract
+
+Each stage workflow must:
+
+1. Include a `workflow_dispatch` trigger (with inputs referenced by the pipeline)
+2. Upload an artifact named `pipeline-compose-<stage-id>` containing `outputs.json` for any output keys listed in the pipeline file
+
+See [docs/examples.md](docs/examples.md) for full stage examples and troubleshooting.
+
+### Permissions
+
+The token passed to `github_token` requires **`actions: write`** to dispatch workflows in the same repository. Release pipelines often also need **`contents: write`**.
+
+### Limitations (v0.1.0)
+
+- Same-repository stages only
+- Each stage runs as a separate workflow dispatch (not inlined jobs)
+- Cross-stage data requires artifact export (see above)
+- `when` expressions support a subset of GitHub expression syntax
+
+### Planned
+
+- Cross-repo stage dispatch
+- Richer expression support
+- Reusable stage catalog patterns

+# pipeline-compose
+
+**Cross-repo CI orchestration that stays inside GitHub Actions.**
+
+`needs:` works great inside one repo. When your release spans a service repo, a QA repo, and an infra repo, you're back to `repository_dispatch`, PAT gymnastics, and tab-hopping across Actions runs with no shared context.
+
+Pipeline Compose gives you one `pipeline.yml`: ordered stages, wait-for-completion, and `context.*` wiring across repos — without Jenkins, without custom polling scripts, without leaving Actions.
+
+**Stable release:** **v1.17.0** — `pipeline-compose local`, standalone `run:` executor, pipeline state store. Cross-repo [GitHub App auth](docs/tutorials/github-app-setup.md) since v1.6.
+
+## The problem
+
+| What you have today | What breaks |
+|---------------------|-------------|
+| `repository_dispatch` | Fire-and-forget. No wait. No outputs back. |
+| `workflow_call` | Same repo only. |
+| PAT maps per target repo | Rotations, least-privilege pain, brittle local tokens. |
+| Bash + `gh run view` polling | Nobody wants to maintain that. |
+
+You don't need a second CI platform. You need **one pipeline graph** that Actions can actually execute.
+
+## What you get
+
+```yaml
+# .github/pipelines/pipeline.yml
+version: 2
+pipelines:
+  release:
+    stages:
+      - id: ci
+        workflow: .github/workflows/ci.yml
+
+      - id: e2e
+        workflow: .github/workflows/e2e.yml
+        repo: my-org/qa-repo
+        needs: [ci]
+        inputs:
+          image_tag: ${{ context.ci.image_tag }}
+
+      - id: deploy
+        workflow: .github/workflows/deploy.yml
+        needs: [e2e]
+```
+
+```mermaid
+flowchart TD
+  ci["ci"]
+  e2e["e2e<br/>my-org/qa-repo"]
+  deploy["deploy"]
+  ci --> e2e
+  e2e --> deploy
+```
+
+**[pipeline-compose-run](https://github.com/aeswibon/pipeline-compose-run)** dispatches each stage, polls until done, downloads `pipeline-compose-<stage>` artifacts, and builds `context` for the next stage. One workflow run. One result.
+
+- **Synchronous** — unlike raw dispatch, the orchestrator waits and fails the pipeline if a stage fails.
+- **Context merge** — stage workflows export JSON via [pipeline-compose-export](https://github.com/aeswibon/pipeline-compose-export); downstream stages read `context.<stage>.<key>`.
+- **Declarative** — graph, `when:`, `needs:`, and cross-repo `repo:` live in YAML, not shell.
+
+No generated workflow to commit unless you choose [pipeline-compose-compile](https://github.com/aeswibon/pipeline-compose-compile).
+
+## Actions
+
+| Action | Repository | Role |
+|--------|------------|------|
+| **Run** | [pipeline-compose-run](https://github.com/aeswibon/pipeline-compose-run) | Orchestrate stages (start here) |
+| **Export** | [pipeline-compose-export](https://github.com/aeswibon/pipeline-compose-export) | Publish `outputs.json` artifact per stage |
+| Compile | [pipeline-compose-compile](https://github.com/aeswibon/pipeline-compose-compile) | Generate a committed workflow from pipeline YAML |
+| Eval | [pipeline-compose-eval](https://github.com/aeswibon/pipeline-compose-eval) | Evaluate `when:` expressions |
+| Context merge | [pipeline-compose-context-merge](https://github.com/aeswibon/pipeline-compose-context-merge) | Manual context JSON without run |
+
+Each action README includes a self-contained glossary.
+
+## Quick start
+
+**1. Pipeline file** — `pnpm run init` scans workflows and writes starter v2 YAML (`.github/pipelines/pipeline.yml`):
+
+```yaml
+version: 2
+companion_workflows:
+  - .github/workflows/release.yml
+pipelines:
+  release:
+    stages:
+      - id: ci
+        workflow: .github/workflows/ci.yml
+      - id: deploy
+        workflow: .github/workflows/deploy.yml
+        needs: [ci]
+```
+
+**2. Export** in any stage workflow that declares `outputs:`:
+
+```yaml
+- uses: aeswibon/pipeline-compose-export@v1.17.0
+  if: success()
+  with:
+    stage_id: ci
+    outputs: '{"image_tag":"${{ steps.build.outputs.tag }}"}'
+```
+
+**3. Entry workflow** (e.g. tag push):
+
+```yaml
+- uses: aeswibon/pipeline-compose-run@v1.17.0
+  with:
+    pipeline_file: .github/pipelines/pipeline.yml
+```
+
+**Cross-repo?** Add `repo: org/repo` on the stage and configure a [GitHub App](docs/tutorials/cross-repo-pipeline.md) (`github_app_id` + `github_app_private_key`) or `repo_tokens_json` on the run action.
+
+Copy-paste examples: [examples/](examples/) · Tutorial: [docs/tutorials/tag-release-pipeline.md](docs/tutorials/tag-release-pipeline.md)
+
+## Developer ergonomics
+
+| Tool | What it does |
+|------|----------------|
+| `validate --strict --workflows` | Schema, DAG, orphans, cross-repo token gaps — fail CI before merge |
+| `validate --simulate` | Dry-run stage table: skips, waves, missing context |
+| `validate --mermaid` | Topology graph for PRs and docs |
+| `catalog` / `catalog_from` | Reuse stage templates; pull catalog from another repo |
+| `import turbo` / `import nx` / `import rush` | Generate pipeline YAML from monorepo task graphs |
+| `smart_rerun` | Re-run failed pipelines; reuse unchanged stages |
+| `context_schema` | JSON Schema for wiring; optional runtime check on export |
+
+PRs that touch pipeline YAML can get a mermaid + simulate + issues comment (see `.github/workflows/pipeline-pr-comment.yml` in this repo).
+
+## Mental model
+
+```mermaid
+flowchart TD
+  py["pipeline.yml"]
+  run["pipeline-compose-run"]
+  sw["Stage workflows"]
+  ex["export artifacts<br/>outputs.json"]
+  ctx["context merged"]
+  inp["next stage inputs"]
+
+  py --> run
+  run --> sw
+  sw --> ex
+  ex --> ctx
+  ctx --> inp
+  inp --> run
+```
+
+**Good fit:** poly-repo release trains, platform-owned stage catalogs, validate-before-merge DAGs.
+
+**Probably not:** single-repo linear CI (native `needs:` is enough), or full deployment-platform features (Spinnaker, Argo CD, etc.).
+
+## CLI (monorepo / local)
+
+```bash
+pnpm run init          # scan workflows → starter pipeline.yml; infers outputs + context_schema from export steps
+pnpm run import turbo  # turbo.json → .github/pipelines/imported.yml (or import nx / import rush)
+pnpm run validate .github/pipelines/pipeline.yml --repo-root . --workflows --strict --mermaid
+pnpm run compile .github/pipelines/pipeline.yml -o .github/workflows/pipeline-generated.yml
+```
+
+See [docs/development.md](docs/development.md) for the full command list and release process.
+
+## Documentation
+
+| Topic | Location |
+|-------|----------|
+| **Design rationale (series)** | [docs/design/](docs/design/) — why this architecture, per-feature decisions |
+| Run + export setup | [pipeline-compose-run](https://github.com/aeswibon/pipeline-compose-run) |
+| Examples (copy `.github/`) | [examples/](examples/) |
+| Tag release walkthrough | [docs/tutorials/tag-release-pipeline.md](docs/tutorials/tag-release-pipeline.md) |
+| Cross-repo `repo:` stages | [docs/tutorials/cross-repo-pipeline.md](docs/tutorials/cross-repo-pipeline.md) |
+| Mermaid topology + PR bot | [docs/mermaid-demo.md](docs/mermaid-demo.md) |
+| Monorepo development | [docs/development.md](docs/development.md) |
+| Glossary | [docs/glossary.md](docs/glossary.md) |
+| **1.0 GA / breaking changes** | [docs/migration/v1.0.md](docs/migration/v1.0.md) |
+| Upgrading from 0.5 | [docs/migration/v0.5.md](docs/migration/v0.5.md) |
+| Pipeline schema (v2) | [packages/core/schema/pipeline-v2.schema.json](packages/core/schema/pipeline-v2.schema.json) |
+| Publishing action repos | [docs/action-repos.md](docs/action-repos.md) |
+
+## Local CI with act
+
+```bash
+pnpm run act:full    # tests, validate, compile parity, bundles
+pnpm run act:ci      # unit tests + build
+```
+
+Requires [Docker](https://docs.docker.com/get-docker/) and [act](https://github.com/nektos/act). See [.github/act/README.md](.github/act/README.md).

+# Action repositories
+
+Each GitHub Action is published from its **own repository** with `action.yml` at the repo root (required for GitHub Marketplace). Source for all actions lives in this monorepo under `packages/action-*`.
+
+| GitHub repository | Monorepo package | Role |
+|-------------------|------------------|------|
+| [pipeline-compose-run](https://github.com/aeswibon/pipeline-compose-run) | `packages/action-run` | Primary runtime orchestrator |
+| [pipeline-compose-export](https://github.com/aeswibon/pipeline-compose-export) | `packages/action-export` | Stage output artifact upload (Node 24) |
+| [pipeline-compose-compile](https://github.com/aeswibon/pipeline-compose-compile) | `packages/action-compile` | Optional static workflow codegen |
+| [pipeline-compose-eval](https://github.com/aeswibon/pipeline-compose-eval) | `packages/action-eval` | `when:` expression evaluation |
+| [pipeline-compose-context-merge](https://github.com/aeswibon/pipeline-compose-context-merge) | `packages/action-context-merge` | Context merge helper (Node 24) |
+
+This repo (**pipeline-compose**) is the single development surface: shared core, CLI, action sources, schema, docs, and release workflows.
+
+## Publish from the monorepo
+
+After changing action or core logic:
+
+```bash
+pnpm test
+pnpm run build
+pnpm run publish:actions v0.3.0
+```
+
+On **tag push**, CI runs this automatically as the final release stage (`publish-actions`) after the meta-repo GitHub Release is created.
+
+### CI setup (one time)
+
+Add a repository secret on **pipeline-compose**:
+
+| Secret | Value |
+|--------|--------|
+| `ACTION_PUBLISH_TOKEN` | PAT with `contents: write` on `pipeline-compose-run`, `pipeline-compose-export`, `pipeline-compose-compile`, `pipeline-compose-eval`, and `pipeline-compose-context-merge` |
+
+Fine-grained PAT: grant **Contents** read/write on each action repo. Classic PAT: `repo` scope works if you own all repos.
+
+Manual publish (e.g. after a failed CI stage): [Actions → Publish actions → Run workflow](https://github.com/aeswibon/pipeline-compose/actions/workflows/publish-actions.yml) with the semver (no `v` prefix, e.g. `0.4.1`). The version must **not** already exist on the action repos — tags are **immutable**.
+
+`scripts/publish-action-packages.sh` clones each action repo, copies `action.yml`, `README.md`, and bundled `dist/`, commits on **`master`** (append-only, no force push), creates a **new** tag once, and opens a GitHub Release with CHANGELOG-derived notes. Each commit message records the monorepo SHA it was built from.
+
+Doc or README fixes ship as a **new patch release** (`0.4.1`, `0.4.2`, …): update the monorepo, add a `CHANGELOG` section, tag, and let CI publish. Do not republish an existing action tag.
+
+Optional **use_master** only changes which monorepo commit is checked out before publish (master HEAD vs `v{version}`); it does **not** allow overwriting an existing action-repo tag.
+
+Local publish uses SSH remotes when `GH_TOKEN` is unset; CI uses `GH_TOKEN` from the secret (HTTPS via `gh auth setup-git`).
+
+Requires the [GitHub CLI](https://cli.github.com/) (`gh`) for local runs.
+
+## Release notes
+
+Action releases use the same root `CHANGELOG.md` as the meta repo. When you run `pnpm run publish:actions`, each action gets a GitHub Release whose body comes from `scripts/ci/render-action-release-notes.sh`.
+
+### Per-action subsections (recommended)
+
+Under each `## [X.Y.Z]` section, add a `###` heading named after the GitHub repo:
+
+```markdown
+## [0.3.0] - 2026-06-14
+
+### Changed
+- Monorepo refactor (meta repo summary)
+
+### pipeline-compose-run
+- Rebuilt bundle; fixes dispatch timeout handling
+
+### pipeline-compose-compile
+- Rebuilt bundle from shared core v0.3.0
+```
+
+`publish:actions` picks the matching `### pipeline-compose-run` block for that repo’s release. If a subsection is missing, the **full** `## [X.Y.Z]` section is used instead (fine when all actions ship the same changes).
+
+Each action release also appends a footer linking to the meta-repo tag on GitHub.
+
+### Local preview
+
+```bash
+bash scripts/ci/render-action-release-notes.sh 0.3.0 pipeline-compose-run /tmp/notes.md
+cat /tmp/notes.md
+```
+
+The meta repo must already have a non-empty `## [0.3.0]` section (`require-changelog-section.sh`).
+
+### Release notes only
+
+Tags and publish commits are immutable. To fix release notes after ship, edit the GitHub Release manually:
+
+```bash
+bash scripts/ci/render-action-release-notes.sh 0.3.0 pipeline-compose-run notes.md
+gh release edit v0.3.0 --repo aeswibon/pipeline-compose-run --notes-file notes.md
+```
+
+Do not move or recreate the tag — consumers pin `@v1.16.0` (or another semver tag) to that commit.
+
+## GitHub Marketplace
+
+Publish from each action repo’s **Releases** page (check **Publish this Action to the GitHub Marketplace**). Tags must exist on the action repo (`pnpm run publish:actions` creates them).
+
+## Consumer refs
+
+```yaml
+uses: aeswibon/pipeline-compose-run@v1.16.0
+```
+
+| Action | Ref |
+|--------|-----|
+| Run | `aeswibon/pipeline-compose-run@…` |
+| Compile | `aeswibon/pipeline-compose-compile@…` |
+| Eval | `aeswibon/pipeline-compose-eval@…` |
+| Context merge | `aeswibon/pipeline-compose-context-merge@…` |
+
+### Migration from monorepo paths (v0.1.0)
+
+```yaml
+# before
+uses: aeswibon/pipeline-compose/run@v1.0.0
+
+# after
+uses: aeswibon/pipeline-compose-run@v1.16.0
+```
+
+Legacy split with sibling directories (`../pipeline-compose-run`, etc.) is no longer used — edit and publish from this monorepo only.

+# 01 — Problem and approach
+
+**Series:** [Design rationale](README.md) · **Next:** [02 — Orchestration model](02-orchestration-model.md)
+
+## Executive summary
+
+pipeline-compose exists because **GitHub Actions has no synchronous, multi-workflow, multi-repo orchestration primitive**. Teams already solved pieces with scripts, PATs, and `repository_dispatch`; we productized the smallest layer that closes the gap **without** replacing Actions jobs or introducing a new execution cluster.
+
+---
+
+## Context
+
+### What breaks at scale
+
+| Symptom | Root cause in native Actions |
+|---------|------------------------------|
+| Library PR cannot gate on consumer E2E | No cross-repo `needs:`; status checks are per-repo |
+| Release spans app + infra repos | `workflow_call` does not generalize to arbitrary `owner/repo` dispatch |
+| “Did repo B finish?” custom polling | `repository_dispatch` is fire-and-forget from repo A’s perspective |
+| Pipeline order lives in wiki tables | Graph is implicit across workflow files and human runbooks |
+| Re-run after stage 9 fails reruns 1–8 | No first-class “resume DAG” across separate workflow runs |
+
+These are **coordination** failures, not “GitHub Actions is bad.” Single-repo DAGs with `needs:` remain the right tool inside one workflow run.
+
+### Organizational constraints we optimized for
+
+1. **Incremental adoption** — keep existing stage workflows; add one pipeline file + one run step. No forklift to Buildkite/Argo unless the org already decided that.
+2. **Actions billing model** — stages stay separate runs (visible in UI, billable per workflow). We did not hide work inside one opaque runner.
+3. **Security review friction** — no arbitrary code execution in the orchestrator beyond Node calling GitHub’s REST API; secrets stay in GitHub Actions secret stores.
+4. **Small maintainer surface** — ponytail/lazy-senior posture: prefer platform primitives over custom infra.
+
+---
+
+## Decision
+
+Ship a **declarative pipeline YAML** plus:
+
+| Component | Role |
+|-----------|------|
+| **pipeline-compose-run** | Long-lived orchestrator job: dispatch → poll → merge context → fail parent |
+| **pipeline-compose-export** | Standardized artifact upload per stage |
+| **packages/core + CLI** | Single semantic source: parse, validate, simulate, compile |
+| **pipeline-compose-compile** (optional) | Same semantics, static `needs:` workflow for same-repo teams |
+
+**Non-goals (explicit):**
+
+- Replace GitHub job sandboxing or build caching (Turbo/Nx layer)
+- Host a remote workflow registry (v1.5 catalog is file-local)
+- Guarantee exactly-once side effects across stages (stages own idempotency)
+- Provide a global pause/approve UI (deferred)
+
+---
+
+## Alternatives considered (expanded)
+
+### Monolithic mega-workflow
+
+**Pros:** one run ID, native `needs:`, familiar UI.  
+**Cons:** does not cross repos; YAML size and review noise; couples unrelated teams’ workflows in one file.  
+**Verdict:** fine inside one repo; not the cross-repo product.
+
+### `repository_dispatch` + custom pollers
+
+**Pros:** minimal dependencies; teams already have scripts.  
+**Cons:** every consumer reimplements wait, timeout, context merge, and status aggregation; no shared validate/simulate; on-call debugs bespoke bash.  
+**Verdict:** pipeline-compose **is** the extracted poller—with stable contracts and tests.
+
+### Reusable workflows (`workflow_call`) only
+
+**Pros:** first-class Actions feature for same-repo reuse.  
+**Cons:** cross-repo `workflow_call` is limited; caller/callee versioning is awkward for org-wide graphs; still no merged “pipeline failed” across unrelated entry workflows.  
+**Verdict:** stage workflows may use `workflow_call` internally; orchestration layer stays dispatch-based for repo boundaries.
+
+### Third-party CI (Buildkite, Harness, Argo Workflows, etc.)
+
+**Pros:** mature DAG engines, agents, secrets, observability.  
+**Cons:** net-new platform cost, agent pools, migration; many enterprises are **mandated** on GitHub Actions for audit/compliance.  
+**Verdict:** valid greenfield; we target **Actions-native** incremental fix.
+
+### Compile-only codegen
+
+**Pros:** auditable committed graph; no polling job.  
+**Cons:** cross-repo dispatch in generated YAML still needs token plumbing per target; every pipeline edit regenerates workflow.  
+**Verdict:** ship as **second path**, not the only path — see [04](04-run-path-vs-compile-path.md).
+
+### GitHub App as the product (marketplace install)
+
+**Pros:** best UX for cross-repo auth and future PR bot.  
+**Cons:** large product surface (install flow, permissions docs, support); auth alone does not orchestrate.  
+**Verdict:** v1.6 ships **BYO App** credentials; marketplace App is roadmap — [10](10-cross-repo-authentication.md), [11](11-deferred-and-rejected.md).
+
+---
+
+## Consequences
+
+### What you gain
+
+- **One pipeline outcome** — entry workflow job success/failure reflects all dispatched stages (including cross-repo).
+- **Validated graph** — `validate --strict` catches orphan workflows, broken `needs`, bad context refs before merge.
+- **Opt-in depth** — smart rerun, sub-pipelines, catalog, schema are YAML flags; simple pipelines stay simple.
+
+### What you pay
+
+- **Orchestrator job duration** — run path holds a runner for the whole pipeline (polling). Cost tradeoff vs fan-out visibility.
+- **Artifact ceremony** — every stage with downstream consumers needs export (or equivalent manual upload).
+- **Dispatch requirement** — every stage workflow must expose `workflow_dispatch`.
+- **Cross-repo secrets** — PAT map or GitHub App credentials are operator responsibilities.
+
+### Blast radius
+
+A bug in **run** affects orchestration only; stage workflows are unchanged. A bug in **validate** fails CI early (desired). Core package bugs affect CLI + all actions — hence monorepo + single core — [05](05-monorepo-and-action-repos.md).
+
+---
+
+## Design principles (how we say “no”)
+
+1. **Platform primitives first** — `workflow_dispatch`, artifacts, `concurrency`, REST polling.
+2. **Explicit contracts** — stable validation codes, artifact names, semver on action repos.
+3. **Validate before run** — simulate and schema checks mirror runtime skip/block rules where possible (`packages/core/src/compile/simulate.ts` aligns with orchestrator skip logic).
+4. **Document shortcuts** — `ponytail:` in code names the ceiling and upgrade path.
+
+---
+
+## Adoption guidance (for PE review)
+
+| Org situation | Recommendation |
+|---------------|----------------|
+| Single repo, 3–5 workflows, no cross-repo | compile path or even native `needs:` may suffice; compose adds value via validate + mermaid |
+| 2–5 repos in one release train | run path + PAT map or App; start with one pipeline file in the “driver” repo |
+| Many repos, strict compliance | GitHub App auth; avoid long-lived PATs in `repo_tokens_json` |
+| Already on Buildkite for builds | don’t duplicate build orchestration; use compose only for the Actions-shaped release tail |
+
+**Migration path from scripts:** replace poller scripts with run action one stage at a time; keep `repository_dispatch` handlers until cutover.
+
+---
+
+## Revisit criteria
+
+We would reconsider the whole approach if:
+
+- GitHub shipped **first-class cross-repo workflow `needs:` with context merge** (platform makes us redundant).
+- Polling + long jobs became **prohibitively expensive** vs an official async orchestration API we could await on.
+- Enterprise customers **uniformly** standardized on an external DAG engine and stopped allowing Actions orchestration jobs.
+
+---
+
+## What to read next
+
+- [02 — Orchestration model](02-orchestration-model.md) — runtime loop and failure semantics  
+- [04 — Run path vs compile path](04-run-path-vs-compile-path.md) — choosing execution mode  
+- [11 — Deferred and rejected](11-deferred-and-rejected.md) — what we are not building yet
